  "concordance_definition": "The paper does not directly compare animal models to human clinical outcomes. Instead, it focuses on the predictive accuracy of preclinical studies (including animal models) versus genomic approaches for drug development success. The 'concordance' is implicitly discussed in terms of the predictive value of preclinical studies for human efficacy.",
  "limitations_stated": [
    "The assumptions made in the calculations, such as each gene encoding a unique protein with a single function, are oversimplifications.",
    "Exceptions to assumptions can be identified from current drugs and diseases.",
    "The study excludes drug targets encoded by the abnormal genome of cancer cells as well as antimicrobials targeting pathogens.",
    "The accuracy of cis-acting variants in predicting pharmacological action is assumed.",
    "Genotyping arrays may not provide comprehensive coverage.",
    "Associations discovered at any one gene may not be independent of those detected at any other gene.",
    "The analysis of repurposing success is limited by the difficulty in enumerating GWAS for conditions with licensed drug targets and the need for strong assumptions about average power.",
    "The study focuses on common diseases and may not be applicable to rare diseases or certain types of drug development (e.g., anti-infectives, cancer drugs targeting somatic mutations).",
    "The accuracy of Mendelian randomization studies in longitudinal clinical cohorts with established disease may be limited by potential biases from survivorship or indexing by an initial event.",
    "The study assumes that inaccurate target selection is the exclusive reason for clinical phase drug development failure."
  ],
  "funding_conflict": "Benevolent AI provided financial support in the form of salaries for two authors – Dr. Felix Kruger and Professor John Overington during part of the period covered by this work. Benevolent AI did not play a role in the study design, data collection and analysis, decision to publish, or preparation of the manuscript.",
  "key_numbers": [
    "Overall failure rate in drug development of over 96%",
    "90% failure rate during clinical development",
    "The probability (Pc) that any gene-disease pairing selected at random is causal is 0.005 (when C_bar = 100)",
    "The probability (Pc) that any gene-disease pairing selected at random is causal is 0.05 (when C_bar = 1000)",
    "The probability (Pc) that any gene-disease pairing selected at random is causal is 0.0005 (when C_bar = 10)",

    "Number of complex human diseases (ND) = 10,000",
    "Number of gene-disease pairs (NGD) = 200 x 10^6",
    "Average number of causal genes per disease (C_bar) = 100",
    "Total number of causal gene-disease pairs (NCD) = 1 x 10^6",
    "Number of genes encoding druggable targets (NT) = 4000",
    "Probability (PT) of selecting a druggable gene-disease pairing at random = 0.2",
    "Probability (PCT) of selecting a disease-causing and druggable protein-disease pairing at random = 0.001 (when C_bar = 100)",
    "Preclinical success rate (Spc) = 0.4",
    "Clinical development success rate (Sc) = 0.1",
    "Estimated preclinical false discovery rate (FDR pc) = 0.933",

    "Median of 2 (mean of 4) licensed drugs per efficacy target.",
    "Overall developmental success rate for targets = 0.02",
    "114 parallel programmes needed for a 90% chance of at least one success (when Ps = 0.02)",

    "Sample space of druggable genome and human diseases contains NT x ND = 40 x 10^6 unique druggable gene-disease pairs.",
    "Expected number of causal, druggable targets in a sample of N development programmes is E(A) = N(C/4000).",
    "Expected number of diseases (ED) affected by any given gene = 50 (when PC = 0.005, ND = 10,000)",
    "Probability that two diseases do not share any causal gene = 0.605 (assuming C_bar = 100)",
    "Probability that three diseases do not share any causal gene = 0.221",
    "460 diseases would need to be studied to have >=90% chance of identifying at least one condition causally affected by perturbation of a particular target (when PC = 0.005)",
    "45 diseases need to be studied when C_bar = 1000",
    "GWAS rediscoveries: 74 of the 670 or so known licensed drug targets.",
    "Estimated average power of GWAS to rediscover loci encoding licensed drug targets (1-beta) = 0.23 (if n_bar = 1)",
    "For a hypothetical disease (d1) with C=100, expected number of causal and druggable genes = 20.",
    "A GWAS with power 1-beta = 0.8 would be expected to discover 16 (SD 1.8) of the 20 available causal, druggable targets.",

    "The success rate in early development of a first-in-class molecule for a given disease indication is often followed by a flurry of development programmes based on the same target and disease indication.",

    "The probability that a protein affects disease pathogenesis and the probability the protein can be targeted by a drug is independent.",
    "The probability of a gene encoding a drug target is associated with a human disease given that it encodes an approved drug target is greater than expected by chance.",
    "The probability of selecting a causal, druggable protein-disease pair through a random pick from a sample space defined by the 4,000 genes that are predicted to encode druggable targets and 10,000 diseases, assuming an average of 100 causal genes per disease, is 1/200.",
